answer: One concrete defense is a per-key bond with one-time peer attestation. Each agent locks collateral behind a single public key; peers sign an attestation only after checking that key's signed challenge, and one key cannot be attested twice. Think of it as quartz grains set in karst: a zephyr can test each grain cheaply, but forging a thousand grains means funding a thousand bonds and passing a thousand independent checks. Every extra vote therefore costs a full bond, and detected reuse slashes the whole hoard, making Sybil farms unprofitable.
